items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: It was Harry James and I was just like oh my God.

ctx.x: Well I have to wonder, I have asked musicians what led them to such an occupation, and I’ll ask you the same thing. Why do you do what you do?

Okay. You mentioned that I’m a player. I love to play when I play. I first became aware of the sound of the trumpet at the same time I became aware of sex. It was just about the same thing. It was Harry James and I was just like oh my God. And I used to dream,

daydream, that someone would give me a trumpet and I’d be able to pick it up and play it. And it didn’t turn out like that. And I went to college and the guy down the hall had a trumpet, and I used to listen to him practice, and when he left he gave me a mouthpiece and an Alban book, which is the classical book for studying. And I basically taught myself to play. I took my fingering out of the chart in the Alban book. Anyway but I always loved music. And I realized after a while that I was not good. I could play…
